scope: Bounded process_info/2 error_handler selector against actual owned process state; other information selectors remain profile refusals.
adaptations: Each owned process initializes its atom-only error_handler setting to the native default. Query the actual target state, not a canned response. Custom handler execution and process_flag are not admitted by this slice.

Admit the atom error_handler, empty selector lists and proper lists containing that selector, including duplicates. Preserve singleton tuple versus list result shapes. Other atom/tuple selectors fail the profile explicitly; malformed admitted list shapes and non-PIDs raise badarg. Validate selectors before resolving the PID, including for dead PIDs.

Resolve only namespace-relative internal PIDs through the World-owned table under Engine serialization. Missing or terminal targets return undefined. Read the immediate setting before caller collection; no target heap pointer crosses GC or an unlock.

Charge list parsing, lookup and output construction; checked final storage reservation preserves outstanding heap credit. Build tuples/lists without dynamic scratch and publish after construction. OOM, memory denial and work denial remain distinct from guest exceptions.

Compiler fixtures and independent OTP reference cover self/other/dead queries, lists, empty lists and badarg. Native tests also initialize nondefault private target state to prove real lookup without claiming a process_flag capability; exercise unsupported-selector refusal, moving GC, heap credit, direct and actual-BIF allocation prefixes, every work prefix, result survival and final balance. Shared-worker tests cover exact bytes, budgets, reuse, peer survival and reclamation.
